reasons: Section 17(b) as quoted (p0118) lets Sparkling (the customer) terminate 'at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice' with no stated cause requirement — a genuine convenience right at the 60–90 day fallback notice period, with no early-termination fee or penalty in the cited text.
No Vendor (Garman) convenience right appears; the only Garman triggers referenced are insolvency/uncured material default (p0128), so the rule's walk-away trigger is not present.

Classification as compliant is correct under the playbook's semantics: the clause meets the fallback on material terms, and the shortfalls versus preferred (90 vs 30 days' notice, silence on pro-rata prepaid-fee refund) are minor sub-elements properly noted in the rationale rather than redlined.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment was proposed; the rendered text is identical to the original.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is a phrasing false negative — the clause omits the words 'for convenience' but grants an unconditional at-will termination right, so it does not undermine the finding.
